vol1:fig-prefill-decode.purpose: How do known prompt tokens become persistent cache state, and how does decode reuse it?
storyboard: Prompt tokens enter the original wide prefill block; their cache entries appear.
The first generated token enters the original narrow decode block.
Read retained cache entries, append the consumed token's K/V, and emit the next token.
vol1:fig-prefill-decode.guard: Do not cache an output token before it has been consumed by the model. Reads preserve cached state; diagram speed is illustrative.

vol1:fig-serving-paged-kv-mapping.purpose: How can ordered tokens use separated physical cache blocks?
storyboard: Follow each logical page through its existing table entry to its physical block.
Read resident K/V records without changing their stored copies; preserve C, D, and the allocated unused tail.
Finish pending accesses, then release E’s private blocks without compacting the pool.
vol1:fig-serving-paged-kv-mapping.guard: Mappings name blocks; they do not carry K/V payload. Two records per block is an illustrative capacity. The lower pool is an after-release reference, not a second live allocation.

vol1:fig-weight-activations-quantization.purpose: Why do INT8 operands need a wider accumulator and an explicit conversion back to INT8?
storyboard: Place real values and integer codes inside the two original input branches.
Follow their existing arrows into multiplication and update the original INT32 output.
Requantize the complete sum, apply the declared activation, then write the output.
vol1:fig-weight-activations-quantization.guard: Preserve requantization before activation. Declare the activation worked case; the source curve is not a ReLU drawing.

vol1:fig-tensor-memory-layout.purpose: Where does the same logical tensor value live in each storage order?
storyboard: Select a cell in the original tensor.
Trace its element offset in both original storage strips.
Traverse a logical row and compare address progression.
vol1:fig-tensor-memory-layout.guard: Alternative layouts are not a copy operation. Distinguish element offsets from byte offsets.

vol1:fig-allocator-live-cached-blocks.purpose: Why can a contiguous allocation fail when aggregate reusable capacity is sufficient?
storyboard: Release B while preserving reserved storage.
Reuse part of B for D and release A.
Attempt the original contiguous request against the separated free regions.
vol1:fig-allocator-live-cached-blocks.guard: Preserve address widths and fixed-pool assumptions. Contiguity is virtual-address contiguity.

vol1:fig-im2col-diagram.purpose: How do overlapping patches create repeated values in the unfolded matrix?
storyboard: Select the original two-channel patch.
Copy its values into the corresponding original matrix row.
Advance the patch and expose duplicated source values before multiplication.
vol1:fig-im2col-diagram.guard: The artwork is two-channel although the preceding miniature prose example is single-channel. Retain actual artwork values and shapes.

vol1:fig-tiling-diagram.purpose: How do successive operand tiles update one retained output tile?
storyboard: Stage the original highlighted A and B tiles.
Advance along K and update the same C tile's partial sums.
Write the output only after the reduction completes.
vol1:fig-tiling-diagram.guard: Preserve A, B, and C placement. Transfer counts do not establish measured speedup.

vol1:fig-activation-checkpointing.purpose: Which activations must remain live, and which can be reconstructed from saved checkpoints?
storyboard: Compute the original chain while retaining selected checkpoints and releasing consumed temporaries.
Replay forward from a saved checkpoint to reconstruct a missing segment.
Consume reconstructed values backward and release each after its last consumer; retain computed gradients separately.
vol1:fig-activation-checkpointing.guard: The two source rows are views of the same activation slots. Declare the deterministic toy chain, keep weights fixed, and distinguish activation-slot counts from total training memory or measured speed.

vol1:fig-kv-cache-growth.purpose: Inspect the original multi-batch curves and weight-adjusted memory budget.
storyboard: Select a batch line on the original chart.
Inspect context length, cache size, and remaining budget at a point.
vol1:fig-kv-cache-growth.guard: Use the canonical registry-derived curves. Do not replace the original chart with toy request-memory boxes.

vol1:fig-training-step-memory.purpose: Why does the location of peak training memory change with batch size?
storyboard: Advance through the original forward/backward event axis in both panels.
Expose saved activations and gradients at the selected event.
Compare each panel's peak against its unchanged inference reference.
vol1:fig-training-step-memory.guard: Preserve both batches, component colors, axes, and original computed data.

vol2:fig-ring-allreduce.purpose: How do reduce-scatter and all-gather combine contributions without confusing reduction with copying?
storyboard: Keep the original four GPU cards, chunk rectangles, two phase panels, and wrap-around links.
Follow chunk A through simultaneous reduce-scatter rounds, adding disjoint contributor sets.
Follow the completed sum through all-gather rounds; copy it unchanged to the remaining ranks.
vol2:fig-ring-allreduce.guard: Never add during all-gather. Preserve original source links and panel geometry; illustrative motion is not a measured network timing model.

vol2:fig-inference-lifecycle.purpose: Follow consumed-position KV state through prefill and decode.
vol2:fig-inference-lifecycle.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol2:fig-paged-attention.purpose: Follow block-table mappings to noncontiguous physical KV blocks.
vol2:fig-paged-attention.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol2:fig-fsdp-parameter-lifetime.purpose: Distinguish persistent shards from temporary gathered parameters and their last consumers.
vol2:fig-fsdp-parameter-lifetime.guard: The original phase grid records history; the separate Live now view shows current residency. Columns are neither addresses nor proportional durations. Optional prefetch is shown as a possibility, not executed.
storyboard: Gather full parameters for forward computation while persistent shards remain resident.
Release gathered parameters while saved activations remain; gather parameters again for backward.
Release consumed parameters and activations while the full gradient remains, then reduce-scatter it into a shard.

vol2:fig-storage-checkpoint-staging.purpose: Why does training resume before the next checkpoint becomes a committed restore point?
storyboard: Capture an immutable snapshot and acknowledge all required local NVMe writes before resuming training.
Copy the staged shards while live training advances; acknowledge durable writes separately and verify the complete set.
Publish the named manifest atomically, then switch the restore point and release local staging.
vol2:fig-storage-checkpoint-staging.guard: Use the source local-NVMe-first schedule, not the separate DRAM-first design described later. Pending writes, durable shard data, verified data, and a published restorable generation are distinct states.

vol4:fig-09-ray-update-epochs.purpose: Which map cells receive new evidence from one qualified range return, and which retain older evidence?
storyboard: Retain the original sensor, grid, ray, phantom outline, occupied hit, and hatched region behind it.
Receive a qualified return; advance free-space updates along the crossed cells and retire the phantom.
Mark the hit occupied and publish the map while untouched cells keep their prior evidence epochs.
vol4:fig-09-ray-update-epochs.guard: Logical update order is not flight time or processing time. Publication does not renew untouched cells; never infer free space behind the hit.

vol4:fig-08-shared-capture-buffer.purpose: Distinguish mapping from copying and release a shared capture buffer after its last consumer.
vol4:fig-08-shared-capture-buffer.guard: Mapping does not copy payload. Conversion may require separate output storage. DMA completion alone does not authorize reuse; outstanding consumers and device ordering still matter.
storyboard: Compare explicit payload copies with shared capture pages as alternative designs.
Complete DMA and admit ordered reads through mappings of A; conversion writes separate storage B for the same frame.
Release each consumer, requeue A after its last release, and inspect B retaining the frame.

vol4:fig-03-request-local-prefill-decode.purpose: Follow one request-local growing KV cache; treat a new observation as new context.
vol4:fig-03-request-local-prefill-decode.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol4:fig-04-multirate-cadence-buffer.purpose: Separate physical clock cadence from event ordering in a shared-buffer handoff.
vol4:fig-04-multirate-cadence-buffer.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol3:fig-vol3-stream-ingestion.purpose: How can bounded head-and-tail capture retain useful process output while discarding an expanding middle?
storyboard: Observed ready bytes travel through the original stdout/stderr paths and adapter into the original head and tail buffers.
After the tail fills, overwrite its oldest slots and increase the omitted-middle count.
Serialize head, omission notice, and chronological tail into the original observation fields.
vol3:fig-vol3-stream-ingestion.guard: Declare toy capacities. Observed readiness does not establish a causal total order between stdout and stderr. Byte caps are distinct from model token budgets; capture excludes full-record, framing, and pipe memory.

vol3:fig-vol3-pagedattention-mapping.purpose: Follow block-table lookup and copy-on-write of a shared tail.
vol3:fig-vol3-pagedattention-mapping.guard: Distinguish table metadata, initialized K/V, and allocated unwritten slots. Reference counts count the two candidate tables, not in-flight consumers. A’s prefix remains unchanged.
storyboard: Resolve an original logical position through its block-table entry and within-block slot.
Fork candidate B’s table without copying the shared prefix; reserve a private tail block.
Copy initialized tail records, remap only B, then append newly computed K/V through a separate inlet.

vol3:fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.purpose: See mixed prefill-chunk and decode work in the canonical iteration schedule.
vol3:fig-vol3-chunked-timeline.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol3:fig-vol3-context-zones.purpose: Why does an unchanged trailing token need new KV state after an earlier prefix change?
storyboard: Process the original cold root, trunk, and leaf while identifying one trailing token T.
Reuse an exact compatible root-and-trunk prefix, then process the changed leaf including unchanged T.
Refresh the trunk, reuse only the root, and recompute all later state; compare T’s new provenance with prior calls.
vol3:fig-vol3-context-zones.guard: Token identity differs from derived KV identity. Historical request rows do not prescribe physical residency or erasure. Prefix reuse also requires compatible resident state; the output reserve is not processed input.

vol3:fig-vol3-idempotency-flow.purpose: Retry the same operation after a lost reply without repeating the side effect.
vol3:fig-vol3-idempotency-flow.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol3:fig-vol3-hierarchical-budget.purpose: Distinguish a local stop from settlement of outstanding child liability.
vol3:fig-vol3-hierarchical-budget.guard: Original-art adaptation proposal; source geometry and rendered states still require review.

vol4:fig-11-intersample-overshoot.purpose: How can valid sampled endpoints conceal a velocity-limit violation between samples?
storyboard: Inspect sampled endpoints on the original velocity curve, then integrate the positive acceleration area toward its hidden peak.
Apply the negative acceleration phase and return to a valid endpoint without erasing the earlier violation.
Use the same acceleration profile from the contracted endpoint baseline and compare the interior peak with the ceiling.
vol4:fig-11-intersample-overshoot.guard: Normalized computed values illustrate the original curve. Preserve equal endpoint velocities and the instantaneous acceleration reversal; this model imposes no finite jerk bound or general motion-safety certification.
